podcast.body: A hit song by the glam band Sweet, which ABBA once considered as an artistic influence during a period of identity uncertainty. "the glam band that had hits with like a fox on the run little Willie."

This song is characterized as a bubblegum classic with all the genre's hallmarks, including alliteration ("Willie drives him silly with his star shoe shimmy shuffle down") and a chant suitable for a roller rink. It was released in Europe in 1972 but not in the US until 1973. Despite its success, the band resented it in the US as they were trying to change their image by then, and deliberately avoided touring the US to support it. "Little Willie has all the markings of the classic bubble gum hit. First is that alliteration. Willie drives him silly with his star shoe shimmy shuffle down."
